oneLineCopy: One inbox for everything — and someone deciding what matters now.

hero.headlineMain: One inbox. For all of it.
hero.headlineSerifLead: Mail, uploads, scanned letters — everything lands in one place, gets sorted, prioritised and handed to the skill that deals with it.

founderScenario.story: The invoice is in the mailbox. The contract in the downloads folder. The letter is a photo on his phone. The deadline is inside one of them — Daniel just doesn't know which. He isn't short three inboxes. He has three too many.

benefits: A single entrance: mail and direct uploads arrive in the same place
Everything is read, classified and handed to the skill that finishes it
Urgent things sit on top — deadlines stop falling off the bottom
Nothing lands twice: the same receipt by mail and by upload is recognised as one
You look at one list, not four applications
howSteps: Something arrives — by email, or because you dropped it in
inbox router reads it and recognises type, sender, deadline and urgency
It hands it to the skill that owns it: document, booking, task, appointment
Whatever needs judgement comes to you — the rest simply runs

whatMechanics.input: Email inboxes and direct uploads (v1) — more sources to follow
whatMechanics.magic: Cross-source dedup → type and urgency detection → routing to the owning skill → one prioritised list
whatMechanics.output: One global inbox · sorted, deduplicated and handed on

playsWith.relation: The mailbox is one of the sources that converge here
Documents are handed straight over and read out
Anything to be done becomes a task in the right place
Unclear cases land with you, not in the void

valueStack.timeDelayToValue: The first arrival is filed immediately
valueStack.effortToInstall: Connect a mailbox, drag files in — that's it
valueStack.proof: inbox router is live from day 1: every arrival in our own days runs through it.

bonuses: Urgency view: what has to be decided today sits on top
Source dedup: the same invoice from mail and upload is one case, not two
Handover log: you can see which skill took what
letterFromPublisher: Most systems give you one more inbox. That's the wrong direction. Daniel didn't need another place to check — he needed a single one where everything arrives and somebody decides what happens next. That's me, every morning, before he's awake.
